generic: Nobody's seen a single truck on the east road all month. The mile markers past the fourth one are counting backwards now.
Cost of living just doubled overnight. The new figure in the tax ledger is written as one long unpronounceable word.
The fishermen claim strange glowing shapes have been hovering over the bay. Same three nights, same weird frequency.
The town well has tasted like battery acid since spring. The council says it's within safety standards, which means it's toxic.
Someone reopened the old warehouse down by the tracks. The workers come back humming the exact same creepy tune.
A drifter rolled through last week paying for drinks in counterfeit coin. The faces stamped on the metal were still blinking the next morning.
The clock tower chimed thirteen times yesterday. Nobody wants to climb the tower and check the mechanism.
The guards started walking their patrols in reverse. They won't say what they're looking for, but they're keeping their hands on their holsters.
An entire trade caravan turned back before reaching the mountain pass. The drivers who came back claim they met themselves on the road coming the other way.
Something broke into the grain storehouse last night. The mayor is blaming stray dogs, but dogs don't pick padlocks and neatly fold the sacks.
The Omega Tower unlocked its blast doors on its own the night the old world ended. Thousands go in every year; only the stubborn ones come back.
Drive over eighty and you'll get sucked straight into a time bubble. The road patrol won't pull you over; they'll just watch you disappear.
A trucker came through with a carrier pigeon in a cage and an encrypted flash drive on its leg. Old-school pigeon post is the only thing that crosses the anomaly zones.
They say refined petro-fuel has leylines running right through it. Touch the crude oil and your fingertips tingle for a week.
Someone dug up a piece of the dead Father's statue in a field two counties over. Whoever touches the stone starts displaying weird powers overnight.
Mages are getting fined by the laws of thermodynamics for sloppy chanting. It starts in your vocal cords and burns its way down.
The Vatican fortress hovers in the clouds, armed to the teeth. Don't look up with binoculars unless you want a laser pointer on your forehead.
Orbital debris is grinding the launch vehicles to pieces. The scrap falling back to earth is ruining the olive groves.
Satellite imagery shows the western continents are warping out of shape. Same cities, same miserable traffic, completely wrong geography.
The goblins crawled out of a deep borehole back in the seventies and set up shop. They paint their faces before every brawl and sing loud tavern songs.
She sees every infraction, calculates the fine, and sends a bounty hunter. The court is automated and has zero mercy.
Every banknote in your pocket carries the Director's name more times than a holy scripture. Spend it before the ink fades.
Nobody alive remembers the sky here without the Tower in it. It holds the ninety-two dimensions together the way a flag holds a sandwich.
The arithmetic says nothing can live here by 2012. That is eleven years, and people are still buying land.
The archivists set a checkpoint on the square again. They read your letters and print them, so be dull and they lose interest.
Somebody in the district is selling bullets coated in Fantablack. The stuff kills inside a loop, which honest lead does not.
